depth_findings.text: D2-199 assumed: turn-timing-v1 stores the WS15-S4 optional failed_attempts_ms and retry_wait_ms as part of its shape; the owner must confirm before MODEL_GATEWAY_RUN_TIMING_PERSIST is switched on, because a gate added later would make it v2.

D11 assumed (recommendation): timing is a RUN_TIMING_RECORDED event (EventType 161, not the reserved 150, which the trace already uses) plus a read over session_tool_audit_intents; the integrator must confirm 161.

D13 assumed (recommendation): a waived run is treated as ZDR at both layers. The gateway never arms or writes for a waived turn, session-core refuses the write, and GetRunTiming returns an empty response for a non-persistent run.

Not live-proven: after a rebuild with all three switches on, one Ask turn and one Do run must each leave exactly one type-161 event with no content columns, GET /api/v1/agents/runs/:id/timing must return them, and a ZDR-TEST org turn must leave a row delta of 0 and get zdr_feature_not_supported/run_inspection from the route.

session-core RecordRunTiming is not behind a session-core switch; only the gateway's MODEL_GATEWAY_RUN_TIMING_PERSIST gates writes. Any owner bearer can write a validated content-free record (max 64 KiB, idempotent per run, request and schema) to its own persistent run.

The Ask-turn arm table in run_timing_persist is process-global, bounded at 4096 and cleared after 30 minutes. A turn armed on one replica whose report is built on another (a resumed stream) is not recorded; this is best effort by design.

There is no end-to-end test that a real Ask stream with the switch on calls RecordRunTiming once with the turn-timing-v1 report, or that a Do stream forwards RunAgentResponse.round_timing. The unit tests cover the switch, ZDR, waived and failure paths and the route only.

Round timing covers only the root loop of one invocation: a continuation or park resume is a new invocation with its own clock and its own round-timing-v1 record, and delegated loops are not listed separately.
The waterfall has no stylesheet yet (classes verevon-chat-waterfall*); the bars inherit currentColor with no set chart height.

depth_findings.text: A plain-reply PDF export clones the live DOM (contentRef -> print.ts element.cloneNode). With the switch on it would copy the widget iframe (still sandboxed) and its toolbar instead of the code block that D2 promises for exports, so the export needs to swap widgets for code before switch-on.

With the switch on, on a second dev server: a slider+SVG widget renders at 1280 and 375 px, light and dark, with origin null; document.cookie throws; fetch is blocked by the CSP; the same text in a Space room post shows code.

The theme is read once, when a widget's srcdoc is first built, so switching light/dark leaves widgets already on screen in the old theme until they remount. S3's host-to-frame theme message should fix this.

When a 9th widget mounts, the oldest live frame is torn down and its state is lost. The window is based on mount order, not thread position, so a history page loaded later could change which widgets are counted as newest.

Under VITE_CHAT_RENDER_LEGACY=true each token rebuilds every markdown block, so a closed widget's iframe would reload on every token while the rest of the answer streams. The incremental path keeps sealed blocks and has no such reload.
Escape closes the large view only while focus is on the host toolbar. A keypress inside the opaque frame does not bubble to the host, so S3 could add a close request over the bridge.

results.notes:
I wrote the code and tests but ran nothing: no cargo, fmt or clippy. The new file and both edits are CRLF, like their sibling files.

What was built:
- **New domain `agent_api.rs`.** It serves the six S3 routes under `/api/agent/v1/*` and forwards them to model-gateway `/v1/agent/*`.
- **Switch.** `GATEWAY_AGENT_API_ENABLED` is read once when the router is built, and only the literal `true` turns it on. Off, `router()` returns an empty `Router`, so the gateway answers exactly as before. I read the switch in `router()` and not in `config.rs` (not my file); tests call `router_with(...)` directly, so no test races on the env var.
- **No caller header reaches model-gateway.** The upstream request is built from an allow-list: the exchanged bearers (`Authorization`, `x-session-authorization`, plus `x-inference-authorization` on the start route only), `Last-Event-ID` on the event stream (checked first), and the request id.
- **Exchange.** `ApiKeyExchangeClient` calls `POST {auth_core_url}/api/{aud}/api-key-exchange` with `x-service-id` and `x-service-api-key`, body `{apiKey, orgId, scopes:["agent:runs"]}`. The credential is the `verevon-gateway` registry principal's `consumerEnv`, `MAIL_TASK_GATEWAY_BRIDGE_SERVICE_API_KEY`; that principal already lists the three audiences under `apiKeyExchange`. This is the one exchange helper in the crate: INNH-10 GW-1 should add its audiences to `ExchangeAudience` rather than write a second client.
- **Token cache.** Keyed by a domain-separated SHA-256 of the key plus the org and audience, never the raw key. Entries are dropped at `exp - 10 s`, the cache is bounded at 10,000 entries, and a key's tokens are dropped when model-gateway answers 401.
- **Per-key rate limit.** Uses `RateLimiter::from_cache_with_rpm`, keyed `agent_api:<digest>`, set by `GATEWAY_AGENT_API_RPM_PER_KEY` (default 60). It runs before any exchange.
- **Error mapping.**
  - An auth-core refusal maps to `api_key_invalid` (401 or 403 for an org key, org mismatch or ex-member), `agent_api_scope_missing`, `agent_api_disabled`, `rate_limited`, `internal_error` or `upstream_unavailable`.
  - A model-gateway error that already carries an S3 code is passed on with this gateway's fixed message, keeping only the contract's allowed `details` keys with scalar values. Anything else is mapped by status.
  - A 404 with no error code means model-gateway's Agent API routes are switched off, so it answers `agent_api_disabled`.
- **Logging.** The key is never logged; the only log fields are `error_class` and `audience`.

Tests are in `agent_api::tests`:
- `switch_takes_only_literal_true`, `switch_off_route_absent`, `switch_on_full_router_has_no_overlapping_routes` (sets the env var under `TEST_ENV_LOCK` and restores it).

deviations: The S3 spec and golden name only `x-api-key`, but auth-core's exchange (S2) requires `orgId` and checks it against the key's `metadata.org_id`. The gateway therefore needs the organisation from the caller: it reads a required `x-agent-org-id` header and sends it only to auth-core, where it is verified. `x-org-id` and `x-verevon-org-id` could not be used because the global `strip_inbound_identity_headers` middleware removes them first.

The switch and the per-key rate are read from the environment when the router is built, inside `agent_api::router()`, not on `AppState` (`config.rs` is not this slice's file). They are read once at startup, never in a handler.

The gateway does not repeat model-gateway's allow-list of start-body fields: it checks only that the body is a JSON object of at most 256 KiB. model-gateway's S7 owns the allow-list, so the closed field list is not kept in two places.

depth_findings.text: The public contract names only x-api-key, but auth-core's exchange requires orgId, so the ingress requires a caller header x-agent-org-id (checked by auth-core against the key's org binding). Before switch-on, either the spec and golden must list this header or S2 must derive the org from the key.

F2 must show three things: model-gateway receives no x-api-key and no caller Authorization or x-org-id header; a key whose org is ZDR gets 412 zdr_feature_not_supported (feature agent_api) through the ingress; the auth-core audit shows one api_key_token_exchanged event per audience per roughly 110 s of cache, not one per request.

Each exchange calls Better Auth verifyApiKey, which spends the key's own plugin rate limit, so a first start-run spends three verifications (model-gateway, session-core and inference-core tokens). A key with a tight Better Auth limit can be refused with key_rate_limited (mapped to 429) even when the gateway's per-key bucket has room.

The ingress shares the gateway principal credential MAIL_TASK_GATEWAY_BRIDGE_SERVICE_API_KEY (registry consumerEnv of verevon-gateway) with the mail-task bridge, so rotating that credential affects both paths.
Nothing checks that the six axum routes in agent_api.rs match the golden's route list; error_codes_match_the_s3_golden pins only the error table, the auth header and scope, and the prefixes.

Public callers also pass the gateway's global per-IP limiter (GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_RPM) and its browser CORS layer before the per-key bucket. Server-to-server callers are unaffected, but a shared egress IP could be throttled by the IP bucket first.
